uncited: The backward pass computes the gradients of the rasterization loss with respect to the 3D Gaussian parameters (means, scales, rotations, SH coefficients, opacities) and camera settings, enabling end-to-end differentiable training of Gaussian Avatars.

It extends the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting differentiable rasterizer [Parent](4812-3d-2d-hybrid-gaussian-rasterization-with-fallback-sigma.md) to support Time-of-Flight (ToF) phase data and depth, returning gradients for color, phasor, depth, normal, and accumulated opacity channels.
The backward pass reconstructs the forward pass context from saved tensors, restructures arguments for the CUDA kernel, and invokes the C++/CUDA implementation to compute gradients.

**Restore Context**: Retrieve `num_rendered`, `raster_settings`, and all saved tensors (`colors_precomp`, `phasors_precomp`, `means3D`, `scales`, `rotations`, `cov3Ds_precomp`, `radii`, `sh`, `sh_p`, `geomBuffer`, `binningBuffer`, `imgBuffer`) from the autograd context.
**Construct Gradients Tuple**: Return gradients in the order matching the forward pass inputs.
- **Debug Mode**: If `raster_settings.debug` is true, arguments are deep-copied to CPU before invocation.
- **Time Complexity**: Proportional to the number of rendered Gaussians and pixels, similar to the forward pass.
- **Memory Complexity**: Requires storing forward pass tensors for gradient computation.
